item.text:
**1B.7 Research Note: Vladimir Putin in 2024**

Bottom line: the evidence is **mixed but weakly against**. Putin did take at least two technocratic / procedural steps that point toward expertise and discipline, but the overall 2024 pattern still shows a tightly loyalist system, not independent nuclear-security institutionalization.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Slightly for 1B.7 | `Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 01.03.2024 г. № 162` | Kremlin | 2024-03-01 | https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/50378/print | Putin amended military statutes to require commanders to report weapon loss immediately, respond to storage alarms, and specify actions for nuclear, chemical, and biological attack scenarios. This is a real discipline-and-safety measure, though it is broad military governance rather than a dedicated nuclear-safety institution. | 1B.7, 1B.3 |
| Slightly for 1B.7 | `Putin taps economist to run defense` | Reuters / ThePrint | 2024-05-13 | https://theprint.in/world/putin-taps-civilian-economist-to-run-defence/2081878/ | Reuters reported that Putin replaced Shoigu with civilian economist Andrei Belousov “to better utilise defence expenditures and harness greater innovation.” That is the clearest technocratic move in the 2024 security sphere. | 1B.7 |
| Slightly against 1B.7 | `Putin taps economist to run defence` | Reuters / ThePrint | 2024-05-13 | https://theprint.in/world/putin-taps-civilian-economist-to-run-defence/2081878/ | The same report says Shoigu, a long-standing Putin ally, was moved to the Security Council. That suggests the reshuffle preserved a loyalist circle around core security decisions rather than opening independent oversight. | 1B.7 |
| Slightly for 1B.7 | `Rússia faz exercícios militares para testar uso de armas nucleares` | Reuters / UOL | 2024-06-13 | https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/06/13/russia-faz-exercicios-militares-para-testar-uso-de-armas-nucleares.htm | Reuters reported that Russia’s elite nuclear unit would analyze the drills so improvements could be made, and that fake warheads were delivered to forward storage points. This suggests procedural learning and custody handling, but not a deeper institutional reform. | 1B.7, 1B.3 |
| Against 1B.7 | `Expanded meeting of the Ministry of Defence board` | President of Russia | 2024-12-16 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/75887 | Putin said Russia had specified nuclear-use principles, kept non-strategic nuclear forces on constant alert, and continued exercises. That shows continued concentration of nuclear/security decision-making around deterrence and readiness, not a move toward depoliticized expertise. | 1B.7, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.3, 1B.5 |

**Synthesis**

- The **best affirmative evidence** is the March 1 discipline/safety decree and the appointment of a civilian economist to run defense.
- The **best negative evidence** is that Putin still kept core security power inside a loyalist circle and continued to frame nuclear/security decisions through readiness and deterrence.
- I did **not** find clear 2024 evidence of durable institutional changes like independent civilian review, stronger external oversight, or a rebalanced nuclear command structure.
- Search gap: public 2024 evidence is thin on internal staffing and institutional design around Russia’s nuclear command chain, so the record is mostly indirect.
